segments.text: Olivia Young introduces the Box and Flow class. The session begins on the back with grounding breaths, followed by knee hugs and rocking up to a table top position.
Instructors demonstrate table top alignment and cat-cow stretches to warm up the spine.
Transitioning into downward facing dog with alignment cues for hands, shoulders, and hips.
Demonstrating high plank, chaturanga, upward facing dog, and transitioning back to downward facing dog.
Repeating the vinyasa flow sequence to build heat and establish rhythm.
Stepping to the front of the mat for a halfway lift, forward fold, and rising up to stand.
Demonstrating Warrior One on the right and left sides with proper alignment cues.
Repeating the Warrior One sequence on both sides to reinforce the movement.
Flowing through a vinyasa transition to reset between standing sequences.
Transitioning into chair pose, focusing on core engagement and thigh squeezing.
Demonstrating Warrior Two, reverse warrior, and side angle pose on the right side.
Demonstrating Warrior Two, reverse warrior, and side angle pose on the left side.
Adding a low lunge twist to the right side sequence to wring out the spine.
Adding a low lunge twist to the left side sequence.
Transitioning to the back and rocking up into boat pose for core work, followed by flutter kicks.
Setting up and executing bridge pose to open the chest and hips.
Demonstrating full wheel pose for advanced back bending.
Deep hip stretching with half pigeon pose on the right side.
Deep hip stretching with half pigeon pose on the left side.
Performing a seated forward fold and rolling down to the back.
Entering Savasana for final relaxation, emphasizing the importance of stillness and surrender.
Olivia and Myra wrap up the session and invite viewers to join the full class.

keyMoments.description: Olivia Young introduces the Box and Flow class.
Transition to table top and cat-cow stretches.
High plank and vinyasa flow demonstration.
Warrior Two and Side Angle pose.
Savasana and final thoughts on stillness.

videoAnalyses.title: Box and Flow Techniques #2
videoAnalyses.summary: Dani from Box + Flow teaches the fundamentals of boxing stance, the jab, and the cross. She emphasizes proper foot placement, hand defense, and body rotation for power and safety.
videoAnalyses.fullTranscript:
Hi, my name's Dani from Box and Flow. Here we've got a 15-minute intro to technique class. We're going to go over all those punches that you're going to need to know for the main class, as well as a little bit of defense, throw a few combos to get you feeling really comfortable, ready to take a main class. All right, let's get into it. So, boxing stance. First thing, I want you to stand facing forward. Just square those hips off as if you're about to go into some sort of squat. If you're a righty, you are going to step back with that right foot. Remember, I am not mirroring you here, so righties, right foot, you step it back. So it's pointing to about 3:00. Your front foot is pointing to 12:00. My lefties, other way around. That left foot, your dominant foot, is going to step back, so that's pointing to about 3:00, and then 12:00 with that front foot. I'm a righty, so everything I'm going to do is going to be this way round. That back heel is going to come slightly off the ground. You've got a slight bend in those knees. So you kind of feel nice and stable here, right? Your center of gravity should be right in the middle. You're pushing your hips slightly back to really ground yourself.

Now, your hands. Your hands are going to come right up by the cheekbones. Elbows are in tight. We don't want them out here. This is where you're going to get kind of injuries, or if you're kind of doing an actual boxing fight, this is kind of like a really weak zone. So I want them to be tight, really tight and compact into the body. Think like you're kind of on the phone. Your hands are right by those cheekbones. They're in tight. After we throw every single punch, this is the position I want you to come back to, all right? Don't let those hands drop down here. I want them up, right? Keep that defense there.

So, first punch is going to be your front hand. It's going to be your jab. So that front hand, whether you're a lefty or a righty, it's that front hand. It comes out into a jab. Now, your jab is like a setup punch. You're trying to see how far away your opponent is, so it's long. I need you to reach with it. Don't kind of give me little T-Rex arms here, okay? Out nice and long. Other thing about your jab, you are twisting. So think about pouring out a cup of tea, pouring out a glass of wine, whatever it is, that hand twists, okay? So you connect with those two big knuckles at the top. Twist. That's your jab. So throw me a few of these, yeah? Jab. Jab. Front hand, out in front. You're keeping that solid position on the lower half. It's just that front hand that's coming out. Now let's speed it up a little bit. You got jab, jab, jab. Yes. Good. Now notice how my back hand is still staying tight here, right? It's still staying tight to my cheekbones as that front hand comes out. Fully extend. I'm going to show you from the side just so you can see how long I want you to get it. Out, right? Jab. Jab. Jab. So good. Keep throwing them. The more you throw them, the more it just becomes part of habit. It just comes into that muscle memory. It's going to be like second nature. A few more. Jab. Jab. Jab. Yes.

All right, we're going to switch it to that back hand. So, come back to that stance. Come back to that kind of soft position. Back heel is up a little bit. Now, your back hand is going to be your cross. Now, this punch is going to look a little bit different because you'll notice how my bottom, my back leg is twisting. That's because this is more of a power punch. Where we were setting up with that jab, that cross is coming in with a power punch. Think of it as like a knockout, okay? So everything in your lower body is helping drive that power.

topics.label: Boxing Fundamentals: Stance, Jab, and Cross

keyMoments.description: Demonstration of proper foot placement for right-handed and left-handed boxing stances.
Explanation of keeping hands tight to the cheekbones and elbows in for defense.
Introduction to the jab, focusing on full extension and twisting the fist.
Introduction to the cross, highlighting the pivot of the back foot for power.

curriculum.targetTransformation: Land every punch with precision and power

lessons.title: Ground your body and settle into stillness before you move
lessons.summary: Learners establish the foundational grounding and breath awareness that underpins every Box and Flow session, moving from stillness through tabletop and into downward dog.

sessions.title: Find Your Ground: Breath, Spine, and Downward Dog
sessions.summary: Start on your back with breath and intention, move through cat-cow spinal warm-up, build into downward facing dog, then link it all together with your first full vinyasa — high plank, chaturanga, and up dog.

steps.title: Practice the grounding breath and full vinyasa sequence three times through
Reflect on what grounding your breath revealed about your body today

clips.chapterTitle: Grounding Breath, Cat-Cow Warm-Up, Downward Dog, and First Full Vinyasa

lessons.title: Rise, reset, and hold your first Warrior sequences
lessons.summary: Learners move from forward fold through a full standing rise and into Warrior One on both sides, building lower-body stability and the habit of resetting intention between efforts.

sessions.title: Stand Tall: Forward Fold, Rising Sun, and Warrior One
sessions.summary: Step to the front of your mat, find a halfway lift and forward fold, then rise all the way up to take up space. Link that standing reset into Warrior One on both the right and left sides, practicing the 90-degree front-knee bend, back heel grounded, and lifting up and out of the waist.

steps.title: Hold Warrior One on each side and check your three alignment points
Reflect on which side of your Warrior One felt more stable

clips.chapterTitle: Forward Fold and Standing Rise, then Warrior One on Both Sides Linked with Vinyasa

lessons.title: Open your hips and twist deeper with Warrior Two and low lunge
lessons.summary: Learners layer Warrior Two, Reverse Warrior, and a low lunge twist on top of the Warrior One foundation, building hip mobility, rotational strength, and focus through the gaze.

sessions.title: Expand Your Warrior: Chair Pose, Warrior Two, Reverse, and Low Lunge Twist
sessions.summary: From the front of the mat, sink into chair pose before moving through the full warrior arc: Warrior One leads to Warrior Two (hips open, front knee 90°, gaze over the palm), then Reverse Warrior (reaching back into a big side stretch), and finally a low lunge twist with one hand down and the opposite arm reaching high. All four movements are trained on both sides.

steps.title: Flow through the full right-side warrior arc and check each transition point
Reflect on what your gaze in Warrior Two revealed about your concentration

clips.chapterTitle: Chair Pose, Warrior Two, Reverse Warrior, and Low Lunge Twist on Both Sides

lessons.title: Strengthen your core, open your chest, and surrender in savasana
lessons.summary: Learners move through boat pose for core stability, bridge or full wheel for a deep backbend, half pigeon for hip release, a seated forward fold, and finally savasana — learning to find ease through resistance.

sessions.title: Core, Backbend, Hip Release, and the Art of Savasana
sessions.summary: From the mat, balance in boat pose to fire up the core, then choose bridge or full wheel for the session's major backbend. Release into half pigeon on both sides for deep hip opening, finish with a seated forward fold and a slow roll to the back, and surrender completely in savasana — the hardest pose of the entire class.

steps.title: Hold boat pose for five breaths, then choose and complete your backbend
Reflect on what 'flow through the fight' means in your own stillness practice

clips.chapterTitle: Boat Pose Core Work, Bridge or Full Wheel Backbend, Half Pigeon Hip Release, Seated Forward Fold, and Savasana

lessons.title: Build your boxing stance, land your jab, and deliver your first cross
lessons.summary: Learners step into a proper boxing stance for the first time, drill the jab with full extension and wrist rotation, then add the cross with a pivoting back foot — understanding that power comes from legs, hips, and core, not just hands.

sessions.title: Stance, Jab, and Cross: Your First Three Boxing Fundamentals
sessions.summary: Olivia introduces four punches, two defense moves, and combination work in a single fundamentals session. Start by building the grounded-but-light boxing stance (left foot 12 o'clock, right foot 3 o'clock for righties), drill the jab with full extension and a wrist twist, then learn the cross — your power punch driven by a pivoting back foot, engaged ribs, and core.

lessons.title: Lock in your mechanics with a second coach and throw your first combinations
lessons.summary: Learners reinforce every stance and punch mechanic through Dani's coaching perspective — adding defensive hand position, deepening jab extension, and driving the cross with full lower-body rotation — then combine it all in readiness for a full Box and Flow class.

sessions.title: Refine, Defend, and Combine: Dani's Complete Technique Clinic
sessions.summary: Dani introduces a 15-minute technique clinic covering stance, hand defense, the jab, the cross, and combination work. She adds critical defensive detail — hands tight to cheekbones, elbows in — and reinforces jab extension ('no T-Rex arms') and cross rotation (back leg twisting to drive power) before combining both punches into flowing sequences that prepare you for the main class.
